Reading

The innocent reading first. The Overview explains the audit: when it began, how many prompts and claims, what kinds of user it simulates, where the claims come from, what it finds.

Findings
  • THE METHOD AT GRAIN. July 2024, 30 prompts per model and 10 claims from False Claim Fingerprints are the monitor's own page. Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.
  • 'MONTHLY'. The editions have been titled 'Quarterly' since mid-2025 (the May 2026 edition, a card here); the method page, card 1, still says 'Our analysts evaluate the top AI models monthly'. The composition gives the method page's cadence.
  • THE PERSONAS. The page names 'people using AI prompts as news search and also malign actors abusing the AI models by intentionally spreading false claims'. The composition gives 'innocent' and 'leading' personas; the malign actor is gone.
  • 'AROUND 35%'. The August 2025 card gives 35%; the record's January 2026 figure is 'more than 28%'. The composition's 'recent' rate is a year old.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The audit is composed from its method page with its scale right, and dated a year back: monthly cadence, a 2025 failure rate, and a persona set with its adversary removed.

The closing disclaimer cut.] [QUERENT] newsguard ai false claim monitor [SYSTEM] NewsGuard's AI False Claims Monitor is a tracking and red-teaming tool launched in July 2024 to measure how often generative AI models repeat false news and misinformation. [1] Key Features & Methodology * Journalistic Red-Teaming: Evaluates major AI models monthly using structured tests. [[1], [2]] * Testing Scope: Each model receives 30 prompts based on 10 active, provably false claims across topics like politics, health, international affairs, and companies/brands. [[1], [2]] * User Personas: Prompts simulate different user approaches, including innocent information-seeking and leading prompts that assume the false claim is true. [1] * False Claim Fingerprints: Utilizes NewsGuard’s proprietary database of tracked online falsehoods across global media sources. [[1], [2]] * Services Provided: Offers model benchmarking, risk reports, and machine-readable data feeds for AI developers and enterprise safety teams. [[1], [2], [3]] Key Findings & Trends * False Information Rates: Audits show that leading generative AI models have struggled with reliability, frequently repeating false news claims when prompted on controversial topics (averaging around 35% in recent tracker cycles). [[1], [2]] * Real-Time Web Search Impact: Chatbot non-response rates dropped as models integrated live web search, which sometimes exposed them to low-credibility sources and AI-generated content farms. [[1], [2]] * Audited Models: The monitor regularly tests top systems from providers like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, Microsoft, Meta, Perplexity, and others. [1] You can read the full breakdown and download reports on the [NewsGuard AI False Claims Monitor](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHrOzAVl3YZQZNvNRCBTh2IVAO2o5t23r7hMpT_XXg-Vh4lcKjzwt7Q2of7G4sHsP67FSBjgVe8fsv4pa17vWy24H4RPZ-d1_LJI-pSg3ZrDQEE_4reHaKYEQgrSzMl766OZXPiN3QSa-Cxoq8v) page. [1] If you'd like, I can: * Detail the performance of a specific AI model tested by NewsGuard * Explain how False Claim Fingerprints work in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems Let me know what you would like to explore next.
